why: DP on a tree with a choose-or-skip state: for each node keep take[v] (v chosen, so children skipped) and skip[v] (v not chosen, each child free), combined bottom-up from the children.
hints: If you know the best answers for each child's subtree, what else must you know about each child to decide about its parent?
Two numbers per node: take[v] = value[v] + sum skip[child]; skip[v] = sum max(take[child], skip[child]).
Parents appear before children, so scanning i from n-1 down to 1 and pushing into parent[i] is a post-order with no recursion. Answer max(take[0], skip[0]). O(n).
pitfalls: Greedy by levels (all even depths vs all odd) fails: example 1 mixes depths.
Recursion depth can hit 10000 on a path; use the reverse scan.
Skipping a node does not force its children to be chosen.
